t: You're at Cartwright Gardens, a crescent-shaped park and street in Bloomsbury. It's named after John Cartwright, who lived from 1740 to 1824. He was a naval officer and a major in the Nottinghamshire Militia, and a prominent campaigner for parliamentary reform, which earned him the title Father of Reform. His younger brother, Edmund Cartwright, became famous as the inventor of the power loom.
